prompt: For butan-1-ol, write the molecular formula, the condensed structural formula and the empirical formula.
markscheme: Molecular C₄H₁₀O **(A1)**; condensed CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH **(A1)**; empirical C₄H₁₀O (already in simplest ratio) **(A1)**

prompt: Which functional group is present in CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
markscheme: **C.** –COO– between two carbon chains is an ester (ethyl ethanoate).

prompt: State two features of a homologous series and write the general formula of the alkanes.
markscheme: Same functional group and general formula; successive members differ by CH₂; similar chemical properties; gradual trend in physical properties (any two) **(A1)**; alkanes $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$ **(A1)**

prompt: Explain why the boiling points of the alkanes increase with chain length.
markscheme: Larger molecules have more electrons and greater surface contact **(R1)**, so London (dispersion) forces are stronger and need more energy to overcome **(R1)**

prompt: Explain what structural isomers are, and give two isomers of C₃H₈O with different functional groups.
markscheme: Same molecular formula but different connectivity of atoms **(A1)**; e.g. propan-1-ol (alcohol) and methoxyethane, CH₃OCH₂CH₃ (ether) **(A1)**

prompt:
**(a)** Explain why but-2-ene has cis–trans isomers but but-1-ene does not. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why butan-2-ol is chiral. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Rotation about C=C is restricted **(R1)**; in but-2-ene each double-bond carbon has two different groups, but in but-1-ene one carbon carries two H atoms **(R1)**

**(b)** C2 is bonded to four different groups (H, OH, CH₃, C₂H₅), giving non-superimposable mirror images **(R1)**

prompt: The mass spectrum of propanone (M = 58) shows major peaks at $m/z$ 58 and 43. Identify the species responsible for each.
markscheme: 58: the molecular ion, [CH₃COCH₃]⁺ **(A1)**; 43: [CH₃CO]⁺ after loss of CH₃ (mass 15) **(A1)**

prompt: An IR spectrum shows a broad absorption at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ and a strong absorption at 1700–1750 cm⁻¹. Identify the functional group present.
markscheme: 1700–1750: C=O **(A1)**; very broad 2500–3000: O–H in a carboxylic acid (hydrogen bonded), so the compound is a carboxylic acid **(A1)**

prompt: Predict the number of signals and their area ratio in the ¹H NMR spectrum of ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH.
Predict the splitting of the CH₃ and CH₂ signals in the ¹H NMR spectrum of chloroethane, CH₃CH₂Cl.
markscheme: $n+1$ rule: CH₃ has 2 neighbouring H, so a triplet **(A1)**; CH₂ has 3 neighbouring H, so a quartet **(A1)**

prompt: Compound X, C₃H₆O, shows an IR absorption at 1715 cm⁻¹ and no absorption at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹. Its ¹H NMR spectrum has a single signal. Deduce the structure of X, explaining each piece of evidence.
markscheme:
1715 cm⁻¹: C=O present **(A1)**; no broad O–H band: not an alcohol or acid **(A1)**

One NMR signal: all six H atoms are equivalent **(A1)**, so X is propanone, CH₃COCH₃ (propanal would show three signals) **(A1)**
